sanskrit: vadhārthaṃ cāsya samare sāyakaṃ sūryavarcasam cikṣepa tvarayā yuktas tvarākāle dhanaṃjayaḥ
english: And to slay him in battle Dhanaṃjaya, swift in the hour that called for swiftness, hurled an arrow blazing like the sun.

sanskrit: tam āpatantaṃ vegena drauṇiś ciccheda sāyakam ardhacandreṇa tīkṣṇena sa chinnaḥ prāpatad bhuvi
english: But Droṇa's son, with a sharp crescent-headed shaft, cleft that arrow as it rushed upon him with speed, and so severed it fell to the earth.

sanskrit: athānyad dhanur ādāya sūtaputraḥ pratāpavān karṇo 'pi dviṣatāṃ hantā chādayām āsa phalgunam sāyakair bahusāhasraiḥ kṛtapratikṛtepsayā
english: Then the mighty son of the charioteer, Karṇa, the slayer of foes, took up another bow and, eager to repay blow with blow, covered Phalguna with arrows by the many thousands.

sanskrit: tau vṛṣāv iva nardantau narasiṃhau mahārathau sāyakaughapraticchannaṃ cakratuḥ kham ajihmagaiḥ adṛśyau ca śaraughais tau nighnatām itaretaram
english: Those two great car-warriors, lions among men, bellowing like bulls, with their straight-flying shafts made the sky one mass of arrow-streams; veiled from sight by the floods of arrows, each struck at the other.

sanskrit: pārtho 'ham asmi tiṣṭha tvaṃ karṇo 'haṃ tiṣṭha phalguna ity evaṃ tarjayantau tau vākśalyais tudatāṃ tathā
english: "I am Pārtha—stand and face me!" "I am Karṇa—stand, Phalguna!" Thus challenging each other, they pierced one another with the barbs of their words.

sanskrit: yudhyetāṃ samare vīrau citraṃ laghu ca suṣṭhu ca prekṣaṇīyau cābhavatāṃ sarvayodhasamāgame
english: The two heroes fought in battle with skill, with swiftness, and with grace, and amid the gathering of all the warriors they were a sight worth beholding.

sanskrit: praśasyamānau samare siddhacāraṇavātikaiḥ ayudhyetāṃ mahārāja parasparavadhaiṣiṇau
english: Praised in the fray by the throngs of Siddhas and Cāraṇas, O great king, they fought on, each seeking the other's death.

sanskrit: tato duryodhano rājaṃs tāvakān abhyabhāṣata yattā rakṣata rādheyaṃ nāhatvā samare 'rjunam nivartiṣyati rādheya iti mām uktavān vṛṣaḥ
english: Then, O king, Duryodhana addressed your men: "Guard Rādheya with all your effort! The bull-like Karṇa has told me, 'I shall not turn back from the battle until I have slain Arjuna.'"

sanskrit: etasminn antare rājan dṛṣṭvā karṇasya vikramam ākarṇamuktair iṣubhiḥ karṇasya caturo hayān anayan mṛtyulokāya caturbhiḥ sāyakottamaiḥ
english: Meanwhile, O king, seeing Karṇa's prowess, Arjuna with arrows drawn to the ear sent Karṇa's four steeds to the realm of death with four excellent shafts.

sanskrit: sārathiṃ cāsya bhallena rathanīḍād apāharat chādayām āsa ca śarais tava putrasya paśyataḥ
english: With a broad-headed arrow he swept Karṇa's charioteer from the seat of the car, and covered him with shafts before the eyes of your son.

sanskrit: sa chādyamānaḥ samare hatāśvo hatasārathiḥ mohitaḥ śarajālena kartavyaṃ nābhyapadyata
english: Overwhelmed in the fight, his horses slain and his driver slain, bewildered by the net of arrows, Karṇa could not tell what should be done.

sanskrit: taṃ tathā virathaṃ dṛṣṭvā ratham āropya svaṃ tadā aśvatthāmā mahārāja bhūyo 'rjunam ayodhayat
english: Seeing him thus deprived of his car, O great king, Aśvatthāman took him up onto his own chariot, and once more did battle with Arjuna.

sanskrit: madrarājas tu kaunteyam avidhyat triṃśatā śaraiḥ śāradvatas tu viṃśatyā vāsudevaṃ samārpayat dhanaṃjayaṃ dvādaśabhir ājaghāna śilīmukhaiḥ
english: The king of the Madras pierced the son of Kuntī with thirty arrows, while Śāradvata struck Vāsudeva with twenty and smote Dhanaṃjaya with twelve bee-like shafts.

sanskrit: caturbhiḥ sindhurājaś ca vṛṣasenaś ca saptabhiḥ pṛthak pṛthaṅ mahārāja kṛṣṇapārthāv avidhyatām
english: And the king of the Sindhus with four, and Vṛṣasena with seven, each in turn, O great king, pierced Kṛṣṇa and Pārtha.

sanskrit: tathaiva tān pratyavidhyat kuntīputro dhanaṃjayaḥ droṇaputraṃ catuḥṣaṣṭyā madrarājaṃ śatena ca
english: In like manner Dhanaṃjaya, the son of Kuntī, pierced them in return—the son of Droṇa with sixty-four shafts and the king of the Madras with a hundred.

sanskrit: saindhavaṃ daśabhir bhallair vṛṣasenaṃ tribhiḥ śaraiḥ śāradvataṃ ca viṃśatyā viddhvā pārthaḥ samunnadat
english: Having pierced the lord of the Sindhus with ten broad-headed arrows, Vṛṣasena with three shafts, and Śāradvata with twenty, Pārtha gave a great roar.

sanskrit: te pratijñāpratīghātam icchantaḥ savyasācinaḥ sahitās tāvakās tūrṇam abhipetur dhanaṃjayam
english: Wishing to thwart the vow of Savyasācin, your warriors together rushed swiftly upon Dhanaṃjaya.

sanskrit: athārjunaḥ sarvatodhāram astraṃ; prāduścakre trāsayan dhārtarāṣṭrān taṃ pratyudīyuḥ kuravaḥ pāṇḍusūnuṃ; rathair mahārhaiḥ śaravarṣāṇy avarṣan
english: Then Arjuna brought forth the weapon that cuts on every side, terrifying the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra; yet the Kurus advanced against the son of Pāṇḍu and, upon their costly chariots, poured down showers of arrows.

sanskrit: tatas tu tasmiṃs tumule samutthite; sudāruṇe bhārata mohanīye nāmuhyata prāpya sa rājaputraḥ; kirīṭamālī visṛjan pṛṣatkān
english: Then, O Bhārata, when that terrible, bewildering tumult arose, the diademed prince, far from being dazed, loosed his arrows undismayed.

sanskrit: rājyaprepsuḥ savyasācī kurūṇāṃ; smaran kleśān dvādaśavarṣavṛttān gāṇḍīvamuktair iṣubhir mahātmā; sarvā diśo vyāvṛṇod aprameyaiḥ
english: Seeking to win back the kingdom, Savyasācin, remembering the sufferings he had borne for twelve years at the hands of the Kurus, that great soul, with countless arrows loosed from the Gāṇḍīva, covered every quarter of the sky.

sanskrit: pradīptolkam abhavac cāntarikṣaṃ; deheṣu bhūrīṇy apatan vayāṃsi yat piṅgalajyena kirīṭamālī; kruddho ripūn ājagavena hanti
english: The firmament seemed ablaze with falling meteors, and birds in multitudes alighted upon the corpses, as the diademed hero in his wrath slew his foes with his tawny-stringed bow, the Ājagava.

sanskrit: kirīṭamālī mahatā mahāyaśāḥ; śarāsanenāsya śarān anīkajit hayapravekottamanāgadhūrgatān; kurupravīrān iṣubhir nyapātayat
english: The diademed one, of great renown, conqueror of armies, with his mighty bow struck down with his shafts the foremost Kuru heroes—those mounted on the choicest horses and at the head of the great elephants.

sanskrit: gadāś ca gurvīḥ parighān ayasmayān; asīṃś ca śaktīś ca raṇe narādhipāḥ mahānti śastrāṇi ca bhīmadarśanāḥ; pragṛhya pārthaṃ sahasābhidudruvuḥ
english: And the kings, dreadful to behold, seizing heavy maces, iron bludgeons, swords and spears and great weapons, all at once rushed upon Pārtha in the fray.

sanskrit: sa tān udīrṇān sarathāśvavāraṇān; padātisaṃghāṃś ca mahādhanurdharaḥ vipannasarvāyudhajīvitān raṇe; cakāra vīro yamarāṣṭravardhanān
english: But that hero, the mighty bowman, made those onrushing foes—with their chariots, horses, and elephants, and their bands of footmen—bereft of all their weapons and of their lives, swelling the realm of Yama.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca sa raṇe vyacarat pārthaḥ prekṣaṇīyo dhanaṃjayaḥ yugapad dikṣu sarvāsu citrāṇy astrāṇi darśayan
english: Saṃjaya said: Pārtha, the splendid Dhanaṃjaya, ranged across the battlefield, displaying in all directions at once his wondrous weapons, a sight worth beholding.

sanskrit: madhyaṃdinagataṃ sūryaṃ pratapantam ivāmbare na śekuḥ sarvabhūtāni pāṇḍavaṃ prativīkṣitum
english: As none can gaze upon the sun blazing in the sky at noon, so could no creature look full upon the Pāṇḍava.

sanskrit: prasṛtāṃs tasya gāṇḍīvāc charavrātān mahātmanaḥ saṃgrāme samapaśyāma haṃsapaṅktīr ivāmbare
english: The flights of arrows streaming from the Gāṇḍīva of that great soul we beheld in the battle like rows of wild geese across the sky.

sanskrit: vinivārya sa vīrāṇām astrair astrāṇi sarvaśaḥ darśayan raudram ātmānam ugre karmaṇi dhiṣṭhitaḥ
english: Having warded off on every side the weapons of those heroes with his own weapons, he revealed his terrible self, fixed firmly upon his fierce work.

sanskrit: sa tān rathavarān rājann abhyatikrāmad arjunaḥ mohayann iva nārācair jayadrathavadhepsayā
english: Bewildering those foremost car-warriors, as it were, with his iron shafts, Arjuna pressed past them all, O king, in his longing to slay Jayadratha.

sanskrit: visṛjan dikṣu sarvāsu śarān asitasārathiḥ sa raṇe vyacarat tūrṇaṃ prekṣaṇīyo dhanaṃjayaḥ
english: Loosing his arrows in every direction, his dark-hued charioteer beside him, the splendid Dhanaṃjaya ranged swiftly across the field, a sight worth beholding.

sanskrit: bhramanta iva śūrasya śaravrātā mahātmanaḥ adṛśyantāntarikṣasthāḥ śataśo 'tha sahasraśaḥ
english: The flights of arrows of that great-souled hero, as though wheeling through the air, were seen poised aloft by the hundreds and the thousands.

sanskrit: ādadānaṃ maheṣvāsaṃ saṃdadhānaṃ ca pāṇḍavam visṛjantaṃ ca kaunteyaṃ nānupaśyāmahe tadā
english: The mighty bowman drawing forth his shafts, the Pāṇḍava fitting them to the string, and the son of Kuntī loosing them—of these we could discern nothing then.

sanskrit: tathā sarvā diśo rājan sarvāṃś ca rathino raṇe ākulīkṛtya kaunteyo jayadratham upādravat vivyādha ca catuḥṣaṣṭyā śarāṇāṃ nataparvaṇām
english: Having thrown into confusion all the quarters and all the car-warriors in the fray, O king, the son of Kuntī bore down upon Jayadratha and pierced him with sixty-four smooth-jointed arrows.

sanskrit: saindhavas tu tathā viddhaḥ śarair gāṇḍīvadhanvanā na cakṣame susaṃkruddhas tottrārdita iva dvipaḥ
english: But the lord of the Sindhus, thus pierced by the arrows of the wielder of the Gāṇḍīva, did not endure it, raging like an elephant goaded by the hook.

sanskrit: sa varāhadhvajas tūrṇaṃ gārdhrapatrān ajihmagān āśīviṣasamaprakhyān karmāraparimārjitān mumoca niśitān saṃkhye sāyakān savyasācini
english: He of the boar-banner swiftly loosed in battle at Savyasācin keen shafts—vulture-feathered, straight-flying, like venomous serpents, burnished by the smith.

sanskrit: tribhis tu viddhvā gāṇḍīvaṃ nārācaiḥ ṣaḍbhir arjunam aṣṭābhir vājino 'vidhyad dhvajaṃ caikena patriṇā
english: With three iron shafts he pierced the Gāṇḍīva, Arjuna with six, the horses with eight, and the banner with a single feathered arrow.

sanskrit: sa vikṣipyārjunas tīkṣṇān saindhavapreṣitāñ śarān yugapat tasya ciccheda śarābhyāṃ saindhavasya ha sāratheś ca śiraḥ kāyād dhvajaṃ ca samalaṃkṛtam
english: Arjuna, scattering the sharp shafts sent by the Saindhava, at one stroke with two arrows severed from the body the head of the Saindhava's charioteer and his ornamented banner.

sanskrit: sa chinnayaṣṭiḥ sumahāñ śīryamāṇaḥ śarāhataḥ varāhaḥ sindhurājasya papātāgniśikhopamaḥ
english: Its staff cut through, that great boar of the Sindhu king's banner, shattered and struck by the arrow, fell like a tongue of flame.

sanskrit: etasminn eva kāle tu drutaṃ gacchati bhāskare abravīt pāṇḍavaṃ tatra tvaramāṇo janārdanaḥ
english: At that very moment, as the sun was swiftly setting, Janārdana in haste spoke to the Pāṇḍava:

sanskrit: dhanaṃjaya śiraś chindhi saindhavasya durātmanaḥ astaṃ mahīdharaśreṣṭhaṃ yiyāsati divākaraḥ śṛṇuṣvaiva ca me vākyaṃ jayadrathavadhaṃ prati
english: "Dhanaṃjaya, cut off the head of the wicked Saindhava! The day-maker is about to descend behind the foremost of mountains. Hear, too, my word concerning the slaying of Jayadratha."

sanskrit: vṛddhakṣatraḥ saindhavasya pitā jagati viśrutaḥ sa kāleneha mahatā saindhavaṃ prāptavān sutam
english: "Vṛddhakṣatra, the father of the Saindhava, is renowned throughout the world. After a long age he obtained the Saindhava as his son."

sanskrit: jayadratham amitraghnaṃ taṃ covāca tato nṛpam antarhitā tadā vāṇī meghadundubhinisvanā
english: "And to that king, the foe-slaying Jayadratha, a disembodied voice, deep as the thunder of clouds, then spoke:"

sanskrit: tavātmajo 'yaṃ martyeṣu kulaśīladamādibhiḥ guṇair bhaviṣyati vibho sadṛśo vaṃśayor dvayoḥ kṣatriyapravaro loke nityaṃ śūrābhisatkṛtaḥ
english: "'This son of yours, O lord, shall be among mortals worthy of both your lineages in his virtues—in family, in conduct, in self-restraint, and the rest—foremost of Kṣatriyas in the world, ever honored by the brave.'"

sanskrit: śatrubhir yudhyamānasya saṃgrāme tv asya dhanvinaḥ śiraś chetsyati saṃkruddhaḥ śatrur nālakṣito bhuvi
english: "'Yet as this bowman fights his enemies in battle, an angered foe, unmarked upon the earth, shall cut off his head.'"

sanskrit: etac chrutvā sindhurājo dhyātvā ciram ariṃdama jñātīn sarvān uvācedaṃ putrasnehābhipīḍitaḥ
english: "Hearing this, O tamer of foes, the Sindhu king pondered long, and, tormented by love for his son, said this to all his kinsmen:"

sanskrit: saṃgrāme yudhyamānasya vahato mahatīṃ dhuram dharaṇyāṃ mama putrasya pātayiṣyati yaḥ śiraḥ tasyāpi śatadhā mūrdhā phaliṣyati na saṃśayaḥ
english: "'Whoever, while my son fights in battle bearing his mighty burden, shall cast his head upon the earth—that man's head too shall burst into a hundred pieces; of this there is no doubt.'"

sanskrit: evam uktvā tato rājye sthāpayitvā jayadratham vṛddhakṣatro vanaṃ yātas tapaśceṣṭaṃ samāsthitaḥ
english: "Having spoken thus and set Jayadratha upon the throne, Vṛddhakṣatra went to the forest and gave himself to the practice of austerity."

sanskrit: so 'yaṃ tapyati tejasvī tapo ghoraṃ durāsadam samantapañcakād asmād bahir vānaraketana
english: "That radiant one, O you of the monkey-banner, is even now practicing terrible, hard-won austerity, just outside this field of Samantapañcaka."

sanskrit: tasmāj jayadrathasya tvaṃ śiraś chittvā mahāmṛdhe divyenāstreṇa ripuhan ghoreṇādbhutakarmaṇā
english: "Therefore, O slayer of foes, when in this great battle you have cut off Jayadratha's head with a divine weapon of terrible and wondrous power—"

sanskrit: sakuṇḍalaṃ sindhupateḥ prabhañjanasutānuja utsaṅge pātayasvāśu vṛddhakṣatrasya bhārata
english: "—cast it, O younger brother of the Wind-god's son, still wearing its earrings, swiftly into the lap of Vṛddhakṣatra, O Bhārata, the head of the lord of the Sindhus."

sanskrit: atha tvam asya mūrdhānaṃ pātayiṣyasi bhūtale tavāpi śatadhā mūrdhā phaliṣyati na saṃśayaḥ
english: "But if you let his head fall upon the ground, then your own head too shall burst into a hundred pieces; of this there is no doubt."

sanskrit: yathā caitan na jānīyāt sa rājā pṛthivīpatiḥ tathā kuru kuruśreṣṭha divyam astram upāśritaḥ
english: "And contrive it, O best of the Kurus, that this king, the lord of the earth, may not know of it—having recourse to the divine weapon."

sanskrit: na hy asādhyam akāryaṃ vā vidyate tava kiṃ cana samasteṣv api lokeṣu triṣu vāsavanandana
english: "For there is nothing impossible or undoable for you in any of the three worlds entire, O delight of Vāsava."

sanskrit: etac chrutvā tu vacanaṃ sṛkkiṇī parisaṃlihan indrāśanisamasparśaṃ divyamantrābhimantritam
english: Hearing these words, Arjuna, licking the corners of his mouth, took up an arrow whose touch was like Indra's thunderbolt, hallowed with divine spells—

sanskrit: sarvabhārasahaṃ śaśvadgandhamālyārcitaṃ śaram visasarjārjunas tūrṇaṃ saindhavasya vadhe vṛtaḥ
english: —a shaft able to bear every burden, ever honored with perfumes and garlands; this Arjuna swiftly let fly, bent upon the slaying of the Saindhava.

sanskrit: sa tu gāṇḍīvanirmuktaḥ śaraḥ śyena ivāśugaḥ śakuntam iva vṛkṣāgrāt saindhavasya śiro 'harat
english: That arrow, loosed from the Gāṇḍīva, swift as a hawk, bore off the head of the Saindhava as a hawk carries off a bird from the treetop.

sanskrit: aharat tat punaś caiva śarair ūrdhvaṃ dhanaṃjayaḥ durhṛdām apraharṣāya suhṛdāṃ harṣaṇāya ca
english: And Dhanaṃjaya bore that head still higher with his arrows, to the dismay of his enemies and the joy of his friends.

sanskrit: śaraiḥ kadambakīkṛtya kāle tasmiṃś ca pāṇḍavaḥ samantapañcakād bāhyaṃ śiras tad vyaharat tataḥ
english: Bearing it aloft on a cluster of arrows at that hour, the Pāṇḍava then carried that head beyond Samantapañcaka.

sanskrit: etasminn eva kāle tu vṛddhakṣatro mahīpatiḥ saṃdhyām upāste tejasvī saṃbandhī tava māriṣa
english: At that very moment, O revered one, the radiant king Vṛddhakṣatra, your kinsman by marriage, was performing his twilight worship.

sanskrit: upāsīnasya tasyātha kṛṣṇakeśaṃ sakuṇḍalam sindhurājasya mūrdhānam utsaṅge samapātayat
english: As he sat at worship, Arjuna let fall into his lap the head of the Sindhu king, black-haired and still wearing its earrings.

sanskrit: tasyotsaṅge nipatitaṃ śiras tac cārukuṇḍalam vṛddhakṣatrasya nṛpater alakṣitam ariṃdama
english: That head with its fair earrings fell into the lap of King Vṛddhakṣatra unnoticed, O tamer of foes.

sanskrit: kṛtajapyasya tasyātha vṛddhakṣatrasya dhīmataḥ uttiṣṭhatas tat sahasā śiro 'gacchad dharātalam
english: Then, as the wise Vṛddhakṣatra, his muttered prayers completed, rose up, that head suddenly slipped to the surface of the earth.

sanskrit: tatas tasya narendrasya putramūrdhani bhūtalam gate tasyāpi śatadhā mūrdhāgacchad ariṃdama
english: And then, when his son's head had fallen to the ground from that king's lap, his own head too, O tamer of foes, burst into a hundred pieces.

sanskrit: tataḥ sarvāṇi bhūtāni vismayaṃ jagmur uttamam vāsudevaś ca bībhatsuṃ praśaśaṃsa mahāratham
english: Then all beings were struck with the utmost wonder, and Vāsudeva praised Bībhatsu, that mighty car-warrior.

sanskrit: tato dṛṣṭvā vinihataṃ sindhurājaṃ jayadratham putrāṇāṃ tava netrebhyo duḥkhād bahv apataj jalam
english: Then, beholding Jayadratha, the king of the Sindhus, slain, much water fell in grief from the eyes of your sons.

sanskrit: bhīmaseno 'pi saṃgrāme bodhayann iva pāṇḍavam siṃhanādena mahatā pūrayām āsa rodasī
english: Bhīmasena too, as though signaling to the Pāṇḍava in the fray, filled heaven and earth with a great lion's roar.

sanskrit: taṃ śrutvā tu mahānādaṃ dharmaputro yudhiṣṭhiraḥ saindhavaṃ nihataṃ mene phalgunena mahātmanā
english: Hearing that mighty roar, Yudhiṣṭhira, the son of Dharma, judged that the Saindhava had been slain by the great-souled Phalguna.

sanskrit: tato vāditraghoṣeṇa svān yodhān abhiharṣayan abhyavartata saṃgrāme bhāradvājaṃ yuyutsayā
english: Then, gladdening his own warriors with the clamor of instruments, he advanced into the battle against the son of Bharadvāja, eager to fight.

sanskrit: tataḥ pravavṛte rājann astaṃ gacchati bhāskare droṇasya somakaiḥ sārdhaṃ saṃgrāmo lomaharṣaṇaḥ
english: Then, O king, as the sun was setting, a hair-raising battle broke out between Droṇa and the Somakas.

sanskrit: te tu sarvaprayatnena bhāradvājaṃ jighāṃsavaḥ saindhave nihate rājann ayudhyanta mahārathāḥ
english: Those great car-warriors, O king, seeking with all their might to slay the son of Bharadvāja now that the Saindhava was slain, fought on.

sanskrit: pāṇḍavās tu jayaṃ labdhvā saindhavaṃ vinihatya ca ayodhayaṃs tato droṇaṃ jayonmattās tatas tataḥ
english: And the Pāṇḍavas, having won the victory and slain the Saindhava, then, frenzied with triumph, did battle with Droṇa on every side.

sanskrit: arjuno 'pi raṇe yodhāṃs tāvakān rathasattamān ayodhayan mahārāja hatvā saindhavakaṃ nṛpam
english: Arjuna too, O great king, having slain the king of the Sindhus, did battle in the fray with your warriors, those foremost of car-warriors.

sanskrit: sa devaśatrūn iva devarājaḥ; kirīṭamālī vyadhamat samantāt yathā tamāṃsy abhyuditas tamoghnaḥ; pūrvāṃ pratijñāṃ samavāpya vīraḥ
english: Having fulfilled his earlier vow, the diademed hero scattered them on every side, as the king of the gods scatters the foes of the gods, and as the risen dispeller of darkness dispels the shadows.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca tasmin vinihate vīre saindhave savyasācinā māmakā yad akurvanta tan mamācakṣva saṃjaya
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: When that hero, the Saindhava, had been slain by Savyasācin, tell me, Saṃjaya, what my men then did.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca saindhavaṃ nihataṃ dṛṣṭvā raṇe pārthena māriṣa amarṣavaśam āpannaḥ kṛpaḥ śāradvatas tadā
english: Saṃjaya said: Seeing the Saindhava slain in battle by Pārtha, O revered one, Kṛpa, the son of Śaradvat, was then overcome with wrath.

sanskrit: mahatā śaravarṣeṇa pāṇḍavaṃ samavākirat drauṇiś cābhyadravat pārthaṃ ratham āsthāya phalgunam
english: With a great shower of arrows he covered the Pāṇḍava, and Droṇa's son too, mounting his chariot, charged upon Pārtha, upon Phalguna.

sanskrit: tāv enaṃ rathināṃ śreṣṭhau rathābhyāṃ rathasattamam ubhāv ubhayatas tīkṣṇair viśikhair abhyavarṣatām
english: Those two foremost of car-warriors, from their two chariots, both on either side, rained sharp arrows upon him, the best of car-warriors.

sanskrit: sa tathā śaravarṣābhyāṃ sumahadbhyāṃ mahābhujaḥ pīḍyamānaḥ parām ārtim agamad rathināṃ varaḥ
english: Thus assailed by those two mighty showers of arrows, that strong-armed one, the best of car-warriors, fell into the deepest distress.

sanskrit: so 'jighāṃsur guruṃ saṃkhye guros tanayam eva ca cakārācāryakaṃ tatra kuntīputro dhanaṃjayaḥ
english: Unwilling to slay in battle his teacher's kinsman and the son of his teacher, Dhanaṃjaya, the son of Kuntī, there displayed his mastery of the craft.

sanskrit: astrair astrāṇi saṃvārya drauṇeḥ śāradvatasya ca mandavegān iṣūṃs tābhyām ajighāṃsur avāsṛjat
english: Warding off with his weapons the weapons of both Droṇa's son and the son of Śaradvat, he loosed at the two of them slow-flying arrows, having no wish to kill them.
